summary: J. A. B. van Buitenen was an Indologist and philosopher who earned his doctorate at Utrecht University under Jan Gonda (~1948–1953). He worked at Deccan College (~1953–1956), Utrecht University (1959–1961), and the University of Chicago (1961).
J. B. Disanayaka is a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He held posts at the University of Colombo (~1961–2002) and SOAS University of London (attested 1996).

J. G. Jennings was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He served as Principal of Muir Central College and as Director of Public Instruction for the Department of Public Instruction, Bihar and Orissa (attested 1918).
J. G. de Casparis was an Indologist and historian-archaeologist. He held positions at Leiden University, where he was a professor (attested 1987), and at SOAS University of London (attested 1991).

Religious studies scholar J. Gordon Melton studied at Birmingham-Southern College, Garrett-Evangelical Theological Seminary, and Northwestern University. He founded and directed the Institute for the Study of American Religion (~1969) and held posts at UC Santa Barbara (~1985–2011) and Baylor University (~2011).
J. L. Shaw is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied at Rice University and under Bimal Krishna Matilal. He held a post at Victoria University of Wellington from ~1973 to 2015.
J. M. E. McTaggart was a philosopher who studied at Clifton College (~1882–1885). He held a post at the University of Cambridge from ~1897 to 1923, where he taught Surendranath Dasgupta.
J. N. Farquhar worked in Indology and religious studies. He was educated at Aberdeen Grammar School, the University of Aberdeen (~1883–1885), and Christ Church (~1885–1889).

J. Robert Oppenheimer studied at Harvard, Cambridge, and Göttingen, and studied under Arthur W. Ryder in 1933. He held posts at UC Berkeley (~1929–1947), Caltech (~1929–1947), the Manhattan Project (~1942–1945), and the Institute for Advanced Study (~1947–1966).

J. S. Negi worked in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology, studying under Ram Shankar Tripathi (attested 1977). He conducted research at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (attested 1977) and served as Chief Editor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 1993–2001).
J. S. Pade was an Indologist. He served as a Research Officer at the University of Chicago (attested 1963) and at the Oriental Institute, Vadodara (attested 1966).

J. Thomas Rimer is a scholar of Japanology who studied at Princeton University and Columbia University. He held posts at Washington University in St. Louis (~1971–1985), the University of Pittsburgh (~1987–2007), UCLA, and the University of Maryland, College Park (attested 2006).

Jack Goody was a scholar of history, archaeology, and religious studies. Educated at St Albans School and St John's College (~1938–1946), he held a post at the University of Cambridge from ~1973 to 1984.
Jack Laughlin is an Indology and religious studies scholar who completed his PhD at McMaster University in 1999. He held a post at the University of Sudbury.

Jacob Dalton is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD at the University of Michigan in 2002 under Donald S. Lopez, Jr. He held positions at the British Library, SOAS, Yale University, and UC Berkeley.
Jacob Grimm was a linguist who studied at the University of Marburg (~1802–1805). He held academic posts at the University of Göttingen (~1830–1837) and the University of Berlin (1841).
Jacob Holubeck is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Kirill Solonin (attested 2013).
Jacob N. Kinnard is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies. He has held positions at William & Mary as Assistant Professor of Religion and at the Iliff School of Theology.

Jacob Samuel Speyer was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who completed his Ph.D. at Leiden University under Johan Hendrik Caspar Kern (~1867–1872). He held posts at the University of Amsterdam, the University of Groningen, and Leiden University.

Jacob Wackernagel was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Friedrich Nietzsche and Theodor Benfey at Basel, Göttingen, Leipzig, and Oxford. He held professorships at the University of Basel (1876–1902, 1915–1936) and the University of Göttingen (1902–1915).
